svg.title: Porous salt crust: configuration, salt balance, and soil–crust flux comparison
svg.desc: Editable vector reconstruction. All labels and mathematical symbols are native SVG text; fraction bars, radicals, boxes and arrows are vector paths. No raster images and no embedded fonts. The internal-precipitation contribution to pore-liquid salt storage is negative. Equation 4 uses a near-equilibrium approximation for the porosity-change contribution. Equations 2 and 3 refer to the linear quasi-steady Prat solution with a saturated base and spatially uniform structural coefficients. Eq. numbers are local to this figure.
svg.metadata: {"figure_type": "editable scientific vector diagram", "units": "SI; salt rates per unit projected area", "equations": {"1": "J_s,Gamma^crust = G_top + R_int + dQ_pore/dt", "2": "G_top = eta S", "3": "R_int = (1-eta) S (1-sech(sqrt(Da)))", "4": "dQ_pore/dt approximately equals rho epsilon_t C_t dh/dt - (rho C_eq/rho_cr) R_int + rho integral_0^h epsilon (partial C/partial t) dz", "5": "J_s,Gamma^soil = rho q C_Gamma - rho phi D_eff^soil (partial C/partial z)|_Gamma", "6": "Delta J_s = J_s,Gamma^crust - J_s,Gamma^soil", "definitions": "S=C_eq j/(1-C_eq); eta=sqrt(Da*)tanh(sqrt(Da))/(1+sqrt(Da*)tanh(sqrt(Da))); Da=h^2/ell^2; ell=sqrt(epsilon_s D_eff/((1-C_eq)a_v k_r))"}, "correction": "Restored minus sign before internal precipitation in Eq. 4; approximate equality explicitly shown."}

g.inkscape:label: Panel a — physical configuration and fluxes
Panel b — editable equations and labels
Definitions, assumptions and figure notes
g.text: Fixed base; no interfacial source or storage. Eqs. (2)–(3): linear quasi-steady Prat limit with a saturated base and uniform coefficients.
Eq. (4) uses C ≈ C_eq in the porosity-change term. All salt rates are per unit projected area; upward is positive.
